key_insight: The paper establishes a validated lattice-Boltzmann data pipeline for 3D turbulent obstructed-channel flows to benchmark neural operators on physically grounded CFD surrogate tasks.
engineering_relevance: It provides reproducible, high-resolution training and test data at Reynolds numbers 1,000–10,000, enabling fair comparison of surrogate models for forecasting, super-resolution, and error correction in turbulent flow applications.
method: Generate 3D channel-flow datasets around synthetic obstacle geometries.
Use a cumulant-collision LBM solver and verify against experimental Strouhal, drag, and fluctuation data.
Perform grid-convergence studies at 1024×512×512 to support dataset credibility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous validation against experiments plus comprehensive grid-convergence testing, with planned physics-informed evaluation metrics for turbulent energy cascade fidelity.
watch_item: The main implementation risk is that surrogate performance may look strong on limited benchmarks but fail to generalize across geometries, Reynolds numbers, or turbulence statistics.
paper_title: A Validated LBM Dataset and Pipeline for Surrogate Modeling of Turbulent 3D Obstructed Channel Flows
